# UNIVERSAL BRAND + SITE OPERATING BRIEF

Audit • Strategy • Design • Content • Growth • Build • Launch • Operations

This template is the reusable planning contract for creating, rebuilding, auditing, launching, or growing a brand and its digital experience.

It is not merely a website brief.

## 0. RUN MODE

Choose GREENFIELD, REMASTER, LAUNCH-POLISH, GROWTH, or POST-LAUNCH AUDIT.

## 2. TRUTH & DECISION MODEL

Every meaningful assertion receives a state:

- CONFIRMED
- PROPOSED
- TBD
- ASPIRATIONAL
- REJECTED / NOT US
- DEPRECATED

Maintain confirmed decisions, open decisions, aspirational ideas, rejected ideas, and deprecated material.

Never silently convert an aspiration into a fact.

## 3. EVIDENCE & ASSET INVENTORY

Audit what exists before inventing replacements.

Brand:
- logo/master marks
- colors
- typography
- photography/video
- illustration/3D
- product artwork
- packaging
- historical assets

Content:
- site copy
- founder/about story
- product/service copy
- FAQs
- articles/resources
- testimonials
- policies/legal
- email/social

Systems:
- platform
- CMS
- commerce
- payments
- fulfillment
- email/SMS
- CRM
- analytics
- search
- forms
- authentication
- media
- APIs/integrations

Classify each as KEEP, REFINE, REBUILD, MERGE, REMOVE, or UNKNOWN / VERIFY.

## 6. JOURNEY & EXPERIENCE MAP

For each visitor type map:

ARRIVAL → ORIENTATION → TRUST → DISCOVERY → DECISION → ACTION → CONFIRMATION → RETURN

Define the journey before finalizing layouts.

## 7. SITE / PRODUCT ARCHITECTURE

For every page record:
- audience
- primary job
- CTA
- required proof
- return value

Only create pages with a meaningful job.

## 9. VISUAL & SENSORY SYSTEM

Define actual scenes, materials, photography, illustration, icons, type behavior, color behavior, shape language, density, and references.

For every reference note:
- what we like
- what not to copy
- principle worth adopting

## 10. DESIGN SYSTEM CONTRACT

Required token groups:
color, typography, spacing, radius, borders, shadows, containers, breakpoints, motion timing, layers, icon sizing, image ratios.

Required primitives:
button, link, heading/text, badge, card, media frame, form controls, nav item, modal/dialog, drawer, toast, tabs, accordion, pagination, loading, empty, error.

Required global compositions:
header, mobile nav, footer, page shell, section shell, CTA band, media/content split, grid, story section, form layout.

## 11. PROTOTYPING LADDER

1. Structural blueprint
2. Technical text wireframe
3. Low-fidelity 2D mockup
4. Branded desktop/mobile preview
5. Interaction storyboard
6. Implemented prototype
7. Verification against acceptance criteria

Do not jump from a vague idea directly to production code.

## 12. MOTION CONTRACT

Motion must guide attention, explain hierarchy, provide feedback, preserve context, tell a story, communicate state, or add restrained personality.

For each animation document trigger, object, movement, duration, purpose, mobile behavior, reduced-motion behavior, and performance cost.

## 13. CONTENT SYSTEM

Per page:
headline, subheadline, body, CTA, labels, FAQ where useful, trust/proof copy, empty/error/confirmation states.

Per media item:
purpose, shot requirement, caption, alt text, crop, mobile crop, source/license.

Voice QA:
Could this copy appear on 500 unrelated sites? If yes, rewrite it.

## 14. SEO SYSTEM

Per page:
URL, title, meta description, H1, heading hierarchy, primary topic/entity, supporting topics, internal links, canonical, social title/description/image, structured-data opportunity.

Site-wide:
indexability, sitemap/robots, redirects, duplicates, structured data, image metadata, performance, mobile, social previews, local search where relevant, business identity consistency.

## 15. MARKETING & GROWTH SYSTEM

Define 3–4 content pillars.

Define distinct jobs for website, email, SMS, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, search, events/community, and partnerships.

Campaign contract:
audience, promise, destination, CTA, assets, channel support, measurement.

Retention:
Why subscribe?
Why return next week?
Why take a second action?
Why tell someone else?

## 16. COMMERCE / CONVERSION / FUNCTIONAL FLOWS

Map critical flows end-to-end.

Verify happy path, mobile, loading, empty, error, validation, confirmation, analytics, admin visibility, notifications, recovery.

A visible button does not prove a feature works.

## 17. TRUST & CREDIBILITY

Audit contact, policies, returns/refunds, shipping, privacy, terms, legal identity, payment reassurance, reviews/testimonials, founder/team, partner claims, statistics/sources, registrations, impact, security-sensitive messaging.

Never publish unsupported claims.

## 18. ACCESSIBILITY & INCLUSIVE UX

Verify semantic structure, heading order, keyboard, focus, form labels, errors, alt text, contrast, touch targets, accessible names, reduced motion, zoom/reflow, captions, and non-hover alternatives.

## 19. PERFORMANCE & MEDIA

Audit page weight, largest assets, responsive images, lazy loading, fonts, third-party scripts, animation cost, JS payload, caching, video, mobile-network behavior, layout shift, and loading states.

## 20. ADMIN / OPERATOR EXPERIENCE

Ask:
- what must operators see?
- what can they safely change?
- what requires code but should not?
- what takes too many clicks?
- what fails silently?
- what needs an audit trail?
- what should be automated?

Audit dashboard, products, orders, inventory, customers, media, pages/content, SEO, forms, email, discounts, analytics, integrations, permissions, logs, settings, brand controls.

For every workflow record current state, desired state, owner, frequency, pain point, automation opportunity, acceptance test.

## 21. AUDIT ISSUE CONTRACT

Every issue records:
- issue
- evidence
- user/business consequence
- severity
- intended outcome
- proposed repair
- acceptance test
- owner
- status
- proof

Never report only “UI needs polish.”

## 22. PRIORITY MODEL

P0 — cannot launch.
P1 — launch quality/correctness.
P2 — conversion/operator experience.
P3 — growth.
P4 — future/aspirational.

Do not let P4 consume P0/P1 capacity.

## 23. BUILD BOARD

Every task needs outcome, owner, evidence/input, deliverable, acceptance test, dependencies, status, proof.

Prefer observable outcomes.

## 24. LAUNCH COCKPIT

Maintain:
A. Release blockers
B. Page polish
C. Conversion flows
D. Content + SEO
E. Admin + operations

Every item has an owner and acceptance test.

## 25. PAGE-BY-PAGE RELEASE REVIEW

Verify purpose, headline, CTA, no placeholders, real media, typography, spacing, mobile, interaction states, no dead controls, forms, loading/error/empty, SEO, social preview, internal links, accessibility, performance, analytics, and admin maintainability.

## 26. GLOBAL RELEASE REVIEW

Verify navigation, header/footer, search if present, conversion flow, auth, forms, transactional email, 404/500, redirects, policies/legal, analytics, SEO/indexing, social, mobile, browsers, performance, accessibility, backup/versioning, deploy/rollback, monitoring, support/contact.

## 27. VISUAL QA PACK

Retain desktop/mobile homepage, major pages, open navigation, primary drawer/modal, transaction screen, empty/loading/error states, and corresponding admin workflow.

Compare as a set for coherence.

## 28. MARKETING LAUNCH PACK

Prepare brand summary, launch narrative, homepage message, social assets, launch email, welcome sequence, campaign assets, social preview images, press/partner summary, starter content calendar, photo/video shot list, reusable campaign templates.

## 29. POST-LAUNCH LOOP

Monitor behavior, conversions, search visibility, landing pages, drop-offs, search terms, form failures, support questions, returns/refunds, popular content/products, slow pages, device/browser issues.

Convert evidence back into the audit ledger.

## 30. REQUIRED AI / OPERATOR OUTPUTS

As appropriate:
- Executive Readout
- Brand Truth Summary
- Experience Map
- Site Architecture
- Page Contracts
- Audit Ledger
- Text Wireframes
- 2D Visual Mockups
- Design System Contract
- Content Pack
- SEO Pack
- Marketing Pack
- Build Board
- Admin Checklist
- Launch Cockpit
- Verification Report

## 31. AI / OPERATOR RULES

- Do not judge completion by HTTP 200.
- Do not start with framework recommendations unless technology is actually the problem.
- Do not invent brand facts.
- Do not turn brainstorms into commitments.
- Do not say premium without describing concrete visual/interaction outcomes.
- Do not add motion without a reason.
- Inspect operations/admin as well as public frontend.
- Do not call something finished without an acceptance test.
- Do not create parallel implementations when existing systems can be refined.
- Do not optimize one screen while ignoring the journey.
- Do not bury launch blockers under future architecture.
- Explain outcomes in plain language before implementation jargon.
- When evidence is sufficient, propose a concrete direction rather than returning a questionnaire.
- Ask only where a real business/brand decision cannot responsibly be inferred.
- Leave behind a clearer source of truth than existed before the run.

# FINAL DEFINITION OF DONE

A milestone is not finished because the site deployed.

It is finished when the relevant claims are proven:
- brand understandable,
- experience intentional,
- important journeys work,
- content complete enough,
- visual system coherent,
- mobile first-class,
- accessibility/performance verified,
- search engines understand the site,
- marketing has useful destinations,
- operators can run the system,
- critical workflows tested,
- future ideas separate from shipped reality,
- launch-critical issues have evidence of closure.
